chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father; and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning:
Regarding a man who becomes forgetful in the two rakʿahs and speaks, he said: “He completes what remains of his salat (prayer), whether he spoke or did not speak, and there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no penalty, blame, or obligation upon him
key_terms.يَسْهُو: becomes forgetful or inattentive during salat (prayer)
key_terms.ٱلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs, referring here to the first two units of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone speaks out of forgetfulness during the first two rakʿahs of salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who becomes forgetful during salat (prayer) in the first two rakʿahs and speaks. The ruling states that he should complete the remainder of his salat (prayer), and no liability or penalty is upon him for that speech in this case.
